0.title: Stop rewatching the whole lecture
0.script: Stop rewatching the whole lecture. Write one question you cannot answer. Find that moment in your notes, then answer from memory before replaying.

1.title: Turn one lecture into 5 questions
1.script: One lecture, five questions. Spot five ideas your lecturer repeats. Turn each into a how or why question, then answer from memory.

2.title: The 2-minute active recall test
2.script: Two-minute active recall test. Close your notes. Explain the topic aloud. Then check your notes and fix what you missed.

3.title: Your slides can be a practice test
3.script: Turn slides into a practice test. Hide one slide, write a question about its main idea, then answer before checking it.

4.title: Find the exact minute you missed
4.script: Missed one minute of class? Name the concept, find it in the transcript, replay that moment, and make one flashcard.

5.title: The 3-pass lecture review
5.script: Review a lecture in three passes. First, skim the key ideas. Next, recall them without looking. Finally, answer practice questions.

6.title: Make flashcards that actually test you
6.script: Make flashcards that actually test you. Put one question on the front and one short answer on the back. Split cards that you keep missing.

7.title: Review a lecture in 10 minutes
7.script: Only ten minutes to review? Scan the outline for two. Recall the key ideas for five. Use the last three to fix your gaps.

8.title: Keep a mistake log for exams
8.script: Keep a mistake log for exams. Record every missed practice question. Write why the wrong answer felt right. Retry the question after two days.

9.title: Use a one-page topic map
9.script: Use a one-page topic map. Put the topic in the center, add a few main branches, then explain every connection aloud.

10.title: Try a closed-book brain dump
10.script: Try a closed-book brain dump. Pick one topic and write what you remember for three minutes. Then compare with your notes and fill the gaps.

11.title: Make a confusion list
11.script: Make a confusion list. Write down every fuzzy term. Turn each one into a precise question, then search or replay only that part.

12.title: Explain it like a tutor
12.script: Explain it like a tutor. Pick one concept, describe it without technical words, and revisit the step where you get stuck.

13.title: Study before the lecture starts
13.script: Before your lecture, scan the title and headings. Write two questions you hope it answers. Then listen for those answers.

14.title: Review within a day
14.script: Review within one day. Skim your notes after class, write three questions from memory, and clear up one confusing point.

15.title: Compare two similar concepts
15.script: Compare two similar concepts. Make two columns, write one similarity and two differences, then create a question that tests the contrast.

16.title: Turn headings into a quiz
16.script: Turn your notes into a quiz. Copy three headings. Make each one a how or why question. Answer before reading the section.

17.title: Space out your review
17.script: Space out your review. Test yourself today, again in a few days, then revisit only the ideas you missed.

18.title: Start with practice questions
18.script: Start with practice questions. Try three without notes, mark the steps you guessed, then review those steps and retry.

19.title: Build a one-page exam sheet
19.script: Build a one-page exam sheet. List five key concepts, add an example to each, then cover the page and explain them aloud.

20.title: Use a question parking lot
20.script: Keep a question parking lot. When class gets confusing, note the question and timestamp. Stay with the lecture, then return afterward.

21.title: Draw it from memory
21.script: Draw it from memory. Pick a process, sketch its stages without looking, then check where your diagram breaks.

22.title: Mix two related topics
22.script: Mix two related topics. Shuffle questions from both, then explain why each answer belongs to its topic.

23.title: End with one takeaway
23.script: End every lecture with one takeaway. Write what changed in your understanding. Turn that sentence into a question for next time.
